So financial accounting is compulsory and standardised, cost accounting is voluntary and shaped to the firm. Every 'difference between' question runs along that line.

chapter: Elements of Cost and the Cost Sheet
trick: The cost sheet builds in four fixed stages, and skipping one is where marks go: Prime cost = direct material + direct labour + direct expenses; + factory overhead = Works cost; + office overhead = Cost of production; + selling and distribution overhead = Cost of sales. Selling expenses never touch works cost.

video.query: cost sheet prime cost works cost cost of production format class 12

data.prompt: Build a cost sheet stage by stage.
data.problem: Direct material ₹50,000; direct wages ₹30,000; direct expenses ₹5,000; factory overhead ₹17,000; office overhead ₹12,000; selling and distribution overhead ₹8,000. Profit is 25% on cost of sales.

steps.why: Prime cost is all the direct costs: 50,000 + 30,000 + 5,000 = ₹85,000.

steps.ask: What is the works or factory cost?
What is the cost of production?
steps.why: Works cost plus office and administrative overhead: 1,02,000 + 12,000 = ₹1,14,000.

steps.ask: What is the cost of sales?
steps.why: Cost of production plus selling and distribution overhead: 1,14,000 + 8,000 = ₹1,22,000.
Profit is 25% ON COST, so 25% of 1,22,000 = ₹30,500, and sales = ₹1,52,500. Had it been 25% on sales, the answer would differ — read which base the question gives.

data.answer: Prime ₹85,000; works ₹1,02,000; production ₹1,14,000; cost of sales ₹1,22,000; sales ₹1,52,500.

chapter: Classification of Costs: Fixed and Variable
trick: Fixed cost is fixed in TOTAL and falls per unit as output rises; variable cost is fixed PER UNIT and rises in total. Getting those two the wrong way round is the standard error. Semi-variable costs, like a telephone bill with a rental plus call charges, have one of each inside them.

video.query: fixed variable semi variable cost behaviour class 12 cost accounting

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about cost behaviour.

items.statement: Fixed cost per unit falls as output increases.
items.why: The same total is spread over more units. Total fixed cost stays put; the per-unit figure falls.

items.statement: Variable cost per unit rises as output increases.
items.why: Variable cost per unit stays constant; it is the TOTAL variable cost that rises with output.

items.statement: Factory rent is a fixed cost.
items.why: It is payable whether the factory produces one unit or ten thousand, within the relevant range.

items.statement: A telephone bill with a fixed rental plus call charges is a semi-variable cost.
items.why: It has a fixed component and a variable component in the same bill.

items.statement: At the break-even point, total contribution equals total fixed cost.
items.why: That is what break-even means: contribution has just covered the fixed cost and profit is zero.

items.statement: Direct material is a fixed cost.
items.why: It varies directly with the number of units produced, which makes it the clearest example of a variable cost.

trick: Cost control keeps costs within a standard already set; cost reduction lowers the standard itself, permanently, without harming quality. So control is about not exceeding the target and reduction is about moving the target — that distinction is what the question is testing when both options appear.

trick: One test settles it: can the burden be passed on? If the person who pays it also bears it, the tax is direct — income tax, corporation tax. If the burden is shifted to someone else, usually the customer, it is indirect — GST, customs duty. Impact and incidence fall on the same person for a direct tax and on different people for an indirect one.

items.label: A tax whose burden the seller passes to the buyer

trick: Within a state, the tax splits in two: CGST to the Centre and SGST to the state, half each. Across states, it is a single IGST collected by the Centre. So the question 'which tax applies' is really 'is this an intra-state or an inter-state supply' — decide that first and the answer follows.

video.query: GST CGST SGST IGST intra state inter state supply class 12

data.prompt: Decide which GST applies and split it correctly.
data.problem: A dealer in Kolkata sells goods worth ₹1,00,000 at a GST rate of 18%.

steps.ask: The buyer is also in West Bengal. Which taxes apply?
steps.why: It is an intra-state supply, so the tax is divided between the Centre and the state.
The rate is halved: 9% CGST and 9% SGST.

steps.ask: Now the buyer is in Bihar. Which tax applies?
steps.why: An inter-state supply attracts a single IGST at the full rate, collected by the Centre.
18% of ₹1,00,000 — the total tax is the same, only its division differs.

data.answer: Intra-state: ₹9,000 CGST + ₹9,000 SGST. Inter-state: ₹18,000 IGST. The total burden is identical either way.
